summary.text: A 36-year-old woman, G4P1L1A2, with chronic hypertension, obesity, prior cesarean delivery and history of infertility presented at 23+3 weeks with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy and ultrasound-confirmed demise of one twin, reported to have occurred at 17 weeks. She was taking amlodipine and aspirin. Despite advice for termination, she and her family opted for continuation of pregnancy; she was admitted, monitored with serial ultrasound scans and given antenatal corticosteroids. The pregnancy was prolonged by 10 weeks with expectant management until an emergency cesarean section at 28+3 weeks for preterm premature rupture of membranes. She recovered uneventfully and was discharged on day three without major or postoperative complications.

article_limitations: The article reports one mother and her surviving twin neonate as two annotated patients; the deceased co-twin is described only briefly (demise at 17 weeks, anomalous, sex not determined) and is recorded as fetus-subject facts in the mother record rather than as a patient.
The stated 10-week prolongation is not recomputed from the gestational ages given (demise at 17 weeks, delivery at 28+3 weeks) and its reference point is not stated.
The sentence on serial antenatal Doppler scans refers to "such complications" named in the preceding sentence; only the literal wording is recorded.
